  HILLS  POLICY AND MANAGEMENT

  MEMORANDUM

 TO:  October 7th Permanent Memorial ad hoc (Mayor Friedman and Vice Mayor
  Nazarian)

 FROM:  Nancy Hunt-Coffey, City Manager

 DATE:  October 8, 2024

 SUBJECT:  Review of RFQ for Permanent Memorial for October

At the last ad hoc meeting of the October 7th Permanent Memorial Ad Hoc, there seemed to be
consensus around the following recommendations:
  • Location of the permanent memorial to be at the north/east corner of the intersection of
  Rexford and Burton Way, to the south of the Library.
  • Consideration of permanent honorary street name to be located on Civic Center Drive
  where it meets Burton Way
  • Develop a Request for Qualifications (RFQ) to seek qualified artists to create the
  memorial.
  • Encourage artists to consider incorporating artifacts from the 10/7 attack into the
  memorial.
  • Set the budget for the memorial “all in” costs to be around $500,000.
  • Have the RFQ response period be 1-2 months to allow artists sufficient time to research
  and develop their vision.
  • The memorial would incorporate signage to provide education and background about
  what occurred on October 7th.

Development of the RFQ
Staff has developed a first draft of an RFQ to seek qualified artists to create the memorial
(Attachment 1). RFQs like this have been used to find artists for projects such as the mural
walls in the Children’s area of the Beverly Hills Public Library. As staff developed the RFQ, the
idea came forward that the City may instead wish to seek proposals from qualified curators who
can vet and bring forward qualified proposals from artists. This process was used previously for
the soundwall on north Canon Dr., next to the Metro staging yard (Attachment 2). There are
benefits and drawbacks to both approaches, some of which are:

--An RFQ directly to artists allows the committee to review every response and to cast a wide
net to artists of different standings. If, for example, the Council were interested in possibly
awarding the commission to an up-and-coming artist, this might be the preferred approach. The
drawback might be that the process could take longer as it will take time to vet each proposal.
--An REQ for curators may speed up the process since a curator will likely be able to identify
quickly artists who have experience with carrying out similar projects. Another benefit of having
a curator involved is that they can assist with managing the art project as it proceeds. A
downside could be that fewer artists may be brought forward for selection, and the cost of the
curator would be additive to the project budget.

The ad hoc is encouraged to provide feedback on whether the REQ should focus on procuring
the services of artists or of curators so that staff can finalize and distribute the REQ.
 Community involvement
At the last ad hoc meeting, there was discussion regarding the level of community involvement
in the development of the memorial. There was some discussion about having a committee that
guides the project which includes community members, similar to the 9/11 memorial. There was
also some discussion about the City Council serving as the committee to guide the project. Staff
requests that the ad hoc provide further guidance on this issue. If the committee will include
community members, staff requests direction on how the community members would be
selected, and at what point in the process, they would be involved.

Financing the memorial
At the previous ad hoc meeting, there was discussion about whether to provide fundraising
opportunities for the memorial, so that members of the community could feel that they
contributed to its creation. While the ad hoc indicated that the city would contribute substantially
to the project, the ad hoc is requested to opine on whether fundraising opportunities should be
made available to the community. In general, fundraising involves also allowing for name,
recognition opportunities. As a result, if the ad hoc is interested in providing for fundraising
opportunities, they are also asked to provide feedback on the type of naming opportunities to
occur at this site.

Recommendation
The Council ad hoc members are asked to provide feedback on the following items related to
the permanent memorial:

--Feedback on whether the RFQ should focus on procuring the services of artists or of curators
so that staff can finalize and distribute the REQ.
--Further guidance on level involvement by the community as the memorial develops. If the
committee will include community members, staff requests direction on how the community
members would be selected, and at what point in the process, they would be involved.
--Feedback on whether fundraising opportunities should be made available to the community
along with naming opportunities
--Any other feedback the ad hoc would like to provide on the process.

INFORMATION AND GUIDELINES
PROPOSAL DEADLINE: TBD
 Project Intent:
The City of Beverly Hills seeks to honor the lives Lost in the tragic terror attack against the state of
Israel on October 7, 2023, which profoundly affected our community. In response to this
devastating event, the City installed over 1 ,000 flags in Beverly Gardens Park—one for each
individual murdered, symbolizing our collective grief and solidarity. This temporary memorial
served as a powerful reminder of our shared values and the resilience of our community. In light of
the overwhelming desire expressed by residents for a permanent memorial, we invite qualified
professionals to submit their proposals to design and implement a lasting tribute that will reflect
the significance of this event and honor the memories of those we lost. We look forward to
collaborating with visionary designers who can help us create a meaningful space for reflection and
remembrance.

GeneraL Information:
Project GoaLs
Each proposal should consider the following:
  1. MemoriaL Considerations:
  •  The design should thoughtfully honor the memory of those who lost their lives in the
  massacre on October 7.
  •  The design should evoke themes of remembrance, resilience, hope, and renewal.
  •  The proposal may include the incorporation of an artifact from the events on
  October 7.
  2.  Construction Considerations:
  • Designs should incorporate durable materials that are suitable for a permanent
  outdoor installation.
  •  Designs should account for long-term maintenance requirements and minimize
  vulnerabilities to weather conditions.
  •  Designs should align with the scale and proportions of the designated site, fostering
  a harmonious relationship with the surrounding environment.

Budget
$500,000

Proposal Dead Line
TBD

encompass all associated project costs, including design, travel, materials, installation, protection,
insurance, and any other relevant expenses.

Location:
444 N Rexford Drive

 Dimensions:
The site has a border measuring approximately 481 .4 feet, encompassing a totaL area of roughly

Existing Conditions:
The project site is a small, landscaped area situated on the south side of the Library building,
bordered by Rexford Drive, Burton Way, and Civic Center Drive. This area features three large,
mature trees that provide shade and enhance the aesthetic appeal, alongside several smalLer
plants that contribute to the site’s greenery. The landscape is equipped with an irrigation system to
ensure the health and vitality of the plant life. CurrentLy, the site is home to an art installation titled
“Home,” as well as a concrete sign identifying the Library. This location presents a unique
opportunity to create a meaningful memorial that integrates with the existing landscape while
enhancing the cultural and communal significance of the space.

 1.0  INTRODUCTION

The City of Beverly Hills (City) is soliciting proposals from qualified finns interested in providing
public art development and management consulting services for the City of Beverly Hills for an
art installation on a temporary construction wall at the intersection of N. Canon Drive and Wilshire
Boulevard in Section 2 (Rodeo Station) of the Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation
Authority (Metro) Purple Line Extension project.

The selected consultant will work with the City and stakeholders to select an artist, establish a
budget, determine deliverables, manage the installation, determine maintenance requirements and
recommend timeline and process for future installations.

This RFQ does not commit the City to pay any costs incurred in the preparation and presentation
of submittals or to select any interested firms who respond.

Tentative Schedule

The City has established the following target dates for evaluation and scheduling purposes. The
following dates are tentative, non-binding, and are subject to change with appropriate notice to
prospective responders.

2.0  PROJECT BACKGROUND

Metro is currently undertaking the construction of the Purple Line Extension Project (Project). The
Project area is located in western Los Angeles County and includes portions of the Cities of Los
Angeles and Beverly Hills, as well as an unincorporated portion of Los Angeles County. Two
stations will be located within the City of Beverly Hills, the La Cienega Station and the Rodeo
Station (at the southwest corner of Wilshire and Reeves). The construction is anticipated to take
8 years with the majority of the street level work at the beginning and end.

In response to stakeholder concerns, City Council approved the temporary closure of N. Canon
Drive at Wilshire Boulevard to vehicular traffic. Part of the implementation of this closure is the
installation of a 20 foot high sound wall across N. Canon Drive just north of Wilshire Boulevard
(Figure 1).

This wall is anticipated to be installed in January 2019 and remain up for a minimum of 2 years,
maximum of 6 years. The thoughtful art selection, installation and potential rotation of art on the
north-facing side of this sound wall is anticipated to enhance the aesthetics of the area and
showcase public artwork that will draw tourists, residents, businesses and visitors.

3.0  SCOPE OF WORK

The Public Art Development and Management consultant will assist in the selection of the artist
and assist in installation, maintenance and management of the artwork on the north facing side of
the temporary sound wall at Wilshire Blvd. and N. Canon Drive for between 2 and 6 years.
Covering the north side of the wall facing N. Canon Drive, the art is intended to frame an
aesthetically pleasing cul-de-sac and pedestrian walkway.

The selected consultant’s tasks are expected to include:

1. Work with the City and Stakeholders to recommend appropriate artists
  • Anticipated meetings to include: 2 stakeholder meetings, 2 core group stakeholder
  meetings, 2 City staff meetings, 1 City Council meeting.

2. Work with the City and stakeholders on the specific artwork to be installed
  • Anticipated meetings to include: 1 stakeholder meeting, 1 core group stakeholder
  meeting, 1 staff meeting, 1 City Council meeting

3. Assist the City in contracting with the selected artist(s)

4. Manage the installation of the art considering the vehicular and pedestrian context around the
  art work, including determination of proper surface material and application and lighting
  design guidelines.

RFQ 18-76 N. Canon Wall
  -  —  Public Art Management  Page 3
 5. Determine best practices for changing the art work if desired and potentially manage
  selection and installation of change-outs (additional contract would be negotiated if needed)

6. Work with the City and stakeholders to determine the feasibility of leveraging Augmented
  Reality to add an additional layer of creative / storytelling onto the wall for all or a portion of
  the exhibit.

7. Provide recommendations and work with the City on appropriate public relations activities
  post-installation, including but not limited to events and outreach.

4.0  ELEMENTS OF THE STATEMENT OF QUALIFICATIONS

The Statement of Qualifications must contain sufficient information to enable the City to determine
the merits of the firm. Statement of Qualifications shall not exceed 25 pages (excluding cover
pages and dividers). The Statement of Qualifications must include the following elements:

  1. Firm Organization and Background
  a. Introduction, including firm name, address, telephone number, fax number and
  email address of the person or persons authorized to represent the firm regarding
  all matters related to the Statement of Qualifications.
  b. Brief profile of the firm.
  c. Proposed project team.

  2. Relevant Experience
  a. Description of firm’s qualifications and experience on similar projects.
  b. Provide resumes of proposed project team and relevant key personnel.
  c. Recent public agency projects of a comparable scope.
  d. Demonstration of a minimum of five (5) years of relevant experience.

  3. References
  a. Provide a minimum of five (5) references.
  b. References must include client name, address, and phone number, brief description
  of the project, role/responsibility of firm on project, and the name/phone number of
  the client’s project manager or primary contact.
  c. It is the firm’s responsibility to verify the latest and current contact information for
  all references.

  4. Fee Schedule
  a. Separate sealed envelope titled ‘Fee Schedule’ shall be submitted, including
  estimate and hourly rates.
  b. Fee schedule will be opened after short listing top ranked firms.

  5. Contact
  a.  Proposers shall not contact the City’s Mayor, Councilmembers, or staff during this
  RFQ process regarding the RFQ.

Statement of Qualifications that do not arrive by the specified date and time, currently scheduled
for September 21, 2018 at 2:00 PM, WILL NOT be accepted. Interested firms may submit their
Statement of Qualifications any time prior to the above stated deadline. The Statement of
Qualifications must be prepared in such a way as to provide a straightforward, concise delineation
of capabilities to satisfy the requirements of this RFQ.

Cost and pricing information MUST be submitted in a separate sealed envelope labeled with the
firm name, date and the title of this RFQ.

trevis@beverlyhills.org.

6.0 SELECTION

Selection of the Public Art Management Consultant will be based upon the quality of the Statement
of Qualification, including comprehensiveness and responsiveness to the requirements of this RFQ
and the following criteria:
  • Similar work experience, references and qualifications of the Consultant.
  • Consultant’s knowledge and understanding of the scope of work, the approach and
  methodology that will be used to complete the work.

After the Statements of Qualification are reviewed and selected candidates are interviewed, the
candidate that, in the judgment of the reviewing panel, is the best qualified will be recommended
for further negotiations on a consulting contract. Staff will recommend the contract for approval
by the City Manager.

7.0 TERM OF CONTRACT

City. See Exhibit A for a sample of the City’s contract agreement. Please indicate in your RFQ

  Beverly Hills City Council Liaison / October 7 Monument Committee Meeting

  SPECIAL MEETING HIGHLIGHTS

  Tuesday, October 8, 2024
  3:00 PM

MEETING CALLED TO ORDER
Date / Time:  October 8, 2024 / 3:00 PM
IN ATTENDANCE:  Mayor Lester Friedman, Vice Mayor Sharona Nazarian, City Manager
  Nancy Coffey, Fire Chief Gregory Barton, Police Chief Mark Stainbrook

  1) Public Comment:
  a. Leore: He was the creative director for the temporary flag 10/7 Memorial. He
  believes that there should be some kind of direction about what the memorial is
  and what it should represent to prevent the project from being dragged in several
  directions by competing visions.

  2) Consideration of a Permanent Memorial for the Victims of October 7th Attack in
  Israel:
  a. Presentation by Nancy Coffey:
  i. At the last meeting, the Liaisons discussed:
  1. Placing the memorial on Burton Way next to the library.
  2. Potentially giving Civic Center between Burton Way and 3rd an
  honorary street name.
  3. Creating an RFQ for artists that would have a budget around
  $500,000.
  4. The RFQ would allow for the incorporation of artifacts from 10/7.
  5. The application period for the RFQ would be open for 1-2 months.
  6. Having educational signage at the site about 10/7.
  ii. Staff would like further direction on:
  1. Whether the City should issue an RFQ for artists or for curators.
  a. An RFQ for artists would see the City directly reach out to
  artists and have the Committee or Council directly review
  each application. This may result in increased vetting times
  but would allow for more community involvement with the
  process.
  b. An RFQ for curators would see the City select a curator who
  would then reach out to artists and review their submissions.
  The curator would then present to the Committee the best
  proposals. This would allow for faster vetting times but
  would result in increased project costs due to hiring a
  curator as well as the curator potentially having a different
  vision for the memorial than the community or Council.
 Highlights for October 8, 2024
October 7 Monument Committee

  2. Staff would also like further direction for what the community
  involvement with the project would look like.
  a. A Community Committee would be made up of community
  members, which would raise questions of how they would
  be selected and how large the committee would be.
  b. The alternative to a Community Committee would be a
  Council led process.
  c. Staff would also like further direction on what a community
  outreach process would look like.
  3. Whether to generate funds for the memorial via fundraising and if
  that fundraising would include a naming opportunity.
  b. Both Liaisons would like to have a Council appointed committee created with a
  curator serving in an advisory role.
  c. Mayor Friedman would like to have each councilmember appoint a member to the
  committee as well as some at large community members who would either be from
  the CVB, Chamber, or Rotary. He would also like for the current liaisons to remain
  as a part of the committee.
  d. The project intent would then be determined by the committee.
  e. Both Liaisons would like the committee to have a maximum of 10 people.
  f. Vice Mayor Nazarian supports the idea of fundraising for the memorial.
  g. The liaisons are firmly against naming the memorial for a sponsor but would allow
  for names of donors to be included in a tasteful fashion.
  h. The 9/11 memorial restricts the naming for donors to the periphery of the memorial.
  i. The Liaisons are in support of recognizing donors but having different levels of
  recognition depending on how much they donated.
  j. The Vice Mayor would like an educational section in the memorial.
  k. The Liaisons would prefer the memorial to be on Rexford and Burton Way rather
  than Civic Center and Burton Way, however they do not want to rename Rexford
  with an honorary street name.
  l. If there is an honorary designation, the memorial area could be designated October
  7 Memorial Plaza.
  m. The design of the October 7 Memorial should not overshadow the 9/11 memorial
  across the street.
  n. The proposal for the RFQ and Committee will be presented to the Council on
  November 7, 2024.

  3) Adjournment:
  Date / Time: October 8, 2024 / 3:54 PM
